issues.description: The solution declares the field 'numberOfTutors' as type short, while the problem UML and task descriptions indicate it should be an int. This mismatches the specified attribute type and leads to inconsistent parameter and method signatures (constructor and setter) relative to the exercise specification and likely tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Use int for numberOfTutors in the solution (and template where applicable). Update the field declaration, constructor parameter, and setter/getter signatures to use int so they match the UML and task descriptions.

issues.description: The solution's constructor takes a short for the numberOfTutors parameter, but the problem statement/UML and expected implementation order/types specify an int for that attribute. This creates a constructor parameter type mismatch relative to the specification and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor parameter type for the last parameter (numberOfTutors) to int and update the constructor body accordingly so the signature matches the UML and task expectations.

issues.description: The solution's setter for numberOfTutors is declared to accept a short, while the rest of the exercise (UML, tasks, and typical tests) expect an int parameter. This method parameter mismatch can cause compilation/test failures when test code or students call setNumberOfTutors(int).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the setNumberOfTutors method to accept an int parameter (and update any internal assignments) so its signature matches the UML/spec and typical test expectations.
